chapters.title: Practicalities of Running a DAO
chapters.content:
# Practicalities of Running a DAO Why should you be a founder of an Activity DAO? - There's an activity you already do for free - Example: Nader posting lifting pictures → Weightlifting DAO - You attend Web3 events or build Web3 communities - Example: Berachain events already host basketball tournaments → HoopsDAO - You want to build a more authentic community - Example: Developer workshops aren't a moat for a new Layer 1; you need to build real community - You want to experiment with DAOs and new mechanisms - You have unique insights into mechanisms that can create regenerative systems - You're from a region where the activity is part of the culture - Examples: Waffle DAO in Brussels, Muay Thai DAO in Thailand, BluntDAO in Miami & NY What if I am in an adjacent proejct? if your protocol already incentivises an activity, has an activity that is mascot adjacent, named after an activity, an activity is essential to your company culture then building an activity DAO would be an awesome fit for your IRL go to market strategy
  • Protocol Associated with Activity: for example
    • Sweat gives you points for walking - WalkDAO
    • SushiSwap → could do sushi eating or making meet-ups and seshin aka SushiDAO
  • Company that does activities: - ZoHouse does community based poker games → nice fit for a PokerDAO

Running a DAO is challenging, but it's crucial to stay focused on the mission and priorities. At its core, an Activity-based DAO is straightforward: ensure the activity happens, incentivize those who participate and organize, and maintain a healthy ecosystem of doers, organizers, and funders.

To streamline the process, consider these key questions: - What's the total cost per event, including materials? - What's the ideal number of participants? - How much should each person contribute to make the event viable? - Will you fund through ticket sales, alternative methods, or seek brand-aligned sponsorships? By addressing these points, you'll create a solid foundation for your DAO's success.

---

Example: Hoops DAO:

- Mission: make sure people ball - Needs for Activitiy - Materials: Basketball - Court: outside park more wholesome - could book with existing gym memberships - could book a gym for private veneue - Preperation - Post about events, coordinate if their is a game - Extra: Prizes / Competition 3v3 ---

chapters.title: Measures of Success
chapters.content:
## Measures of Success how you know if your activity dao is working or failing

- [ ] Anyone can easily find people to do the activity and secure sufficient funding in a streamlined fashion. - [ ] At events, people understand how to get involved and the process for self-organizing and obtaining funding is transparent. - [ ] New participants bring in more funding than existing members request. - [ ] Is the activity happening regularly? Are people eager to contribute? How easy is it to find and fund organizers? - [ ] Do people feel connected to your community? Do they identify with the brand, mention it in their bios, and actively engage? - [ ] Is your community fostering healthier relationships, positive business side effects, and collaborations? - [ ] Do community members voluntarily cover the costs for the activity?
